title: VPC offsite deploy — weekly check-in (Apr 6–10, 2026)
body:
Summary:

This week focused on three active customer installations with VPC/on-prem constraints and two recurring platform issues uncovered during canary installs. The tone is operational: lots of short-term fixes, a couple of follow-on engineering tasks for next sprint, and clarifying runbook gaps around network prechecks and driver compatibility.

Attendees (recurring): Asha Patel (owner), Diego Morales (platform eng), Lina Zhang (solutions eng), Marcus Reed (SRE), Taylor (customer lead on AcmeHealth), Jonah (customer lead on FinGrid)

Weekly goals (what we wanted to finish):
- Complete initial on-prem agent bootstrap for AcmeHealth (air-gapped).
- Validate VPC NAT/Egress plan for FinGrid + get firewall rule approvals.
- Debug CUDA mismatch causing worker crash on Customer X PoC cluster.
- Improve install-runbook network precheck steps (add cert checks + bastion validation).

Daily standup highlights and notes:

Mon 2026-04-06
- AcmeHealth: Successfully completed offline bootstrap for agent v2.1.0 using our signed tarball and local apt proxy. Had to work around missing ca-certificates package on their hardened Debian 11 base image. Outcome: agent installed, but TLS handshake failed on connection to customer-side bastion (self-signed CA).
- FinGrid: NAT egress policy draft sent to customer network team. Waiting on RST/ACK port opening confirmation for 443 and 5222 for our health probes.
- PoC cluster: observed OOM in model server process when loading 8-bit quantized model; hypothesis is kernel/driver mismatch.

Blockers identified:
- AcmeHealth handshake fails until CA bundle is added to system trust store (blocked by their security team change window).
- FinGrid firewall needs specific egress permit for our monitoring endpoint; they are requiring justification doc (Taylor to supply by Tue EOD).

Action items Monday:
- Lina to produce a minimal CA installation doc and sample systemd unit to restart agent after cert update (due Tue 04-07).
- Asha to add addenda to runbook describing apt-proxy steps for air-gapped Debian hosts (due Wed 04-08).

Tues 2026-04-07
- AcmeHealth: Security team applied CA bundle in staging, TLS handshake succeeded. Agent begun registration but hung during initial model cache fetch because their outbound proxy blocks unknown SNI. Workaround: use customer host-level proxy socket mapping (we deployed small proxy-forwarder).
- PoC cluster: Marcus reproduced crash locally; root cause narrowed to NVIDIA driver 535 vs agent container expecting 525/CUDA11 libs.
- FinGrid: Customer asked for temporary SSH bastion to perform interactive test. We approved limited-time key; connection test successful.

Decisions made:
- For air-gapped installs where SNI/mTLS is blocked, we will recommend a proxy-forwarder pattern and include a sample systemd + socat configuration in runbook.
- Lock agent baseline to support driver versions 525 and 535 in next release; scheduling patch in sprint planning.

Action items Tuesday:
- Marcus to prepare CI matrix job for container images against NVIDIA drivers 520/525/535 and CUDA 11/12 (due Fri 04-10).
- Diego to add proxy-forwarder example and small config template to runbook (due Wed 04-08).

Wed 2026-04-08
- AcmeHealth: Initial model download completed. Observed degraded throughput vs expected (3x slower token throughput). Investigation points to host CPU steal during kernel crypto ops (their box uses software crypto only).
- FinGrid: Network team approved egress for 443 and a health-check port; they refused 5222 (XMPP) since it's not allowed by policy. We switched health-checks to HTTP(S) on 443 and adjusted agent health endpoint.
- PoC cluster: Temporary mitigation applied by reducing per-worker batch size and enabling KV-cache persistence; reduced crash frequency but not eliminated.

Blockers/risks:
- AcmeHealth throughput SLA concern: requires either hardware crypto offload or quantization profile change (trade-off quality vs latency). Decision pending with customer.
- PoC cluster: Driver mismatch still requires agent/container compatibility patch; untrusted to rollout immediately to all customers without automated testing.

Action items Wednesday:
- Lina to prepare an options memo for AcmeHealth comparing hardware crypto vs model quantization impacts (owner: Lina, due Thu 04-09).
- Marcus + CI to run driver compatibility matrix; coordinate with release-engineering for access to test GPU hosts.

Thu 2026-04-09
- Internal engineering sync: Agreed to backfill tests and bump agent tag to advertise supported driver list in our model catalog. Established acceptance criteria for driver support (no crash in 1000 sample inferences, memory stability, throughput within 15% of baseline).
- AcmeHealth: Customer opted to proceed with quantization fallback for initial rollout to meet latency targets; will reevaluate hardware crypto later. We drafted parameter changes for Optimize team to monitor quality regressions.
- FinGrid: Completed canary deployment; logs show intermittent TLS renegotiation errors from their AWS Transit Gateway. Marcus suspects MTU fragmentation; recommended enabling path MTU discovery and setting agent keepalive to 30s.

Action items Thursday:
- Asha to open a postmortem ticket for FinGrid transient TLS renegotiation and add MTU/keepalive checklist to runbook (JIRA-PD-472, due Mon 04-13).
- Diego to create a small egress justification template we can provide to customers for firewall requests (done; linked).

Fri 2026-04-10
- Runbook updates: merged proxy-forwarder sample, CA-install snippet, and the new network precheck checklist into a draft runbook change (waiting for engineering review).
- CI driver matrix: Marcus initial jobs passed for 525/CUDA11 but failing on 535/CUDA12 due to missing libnvidia-ml symbols in our base image. Identified two remediation approaches: rebuild base image with CUDA12 toolchain OR add a compatibility shim library at container startup.
- Customer X (internal PoC) asked for a documented rollback plan after agent upgrade; created rollback playbook skeleton and tested rollback on staging.

Open technical follow-ups and owners:
- Driver compatibility patch/decision: Marcus + release-eng to recommend build vs shim (owner: Marcus, due Tue 04-14).
- Runbook finalization and publish: Diego + Lina to complete review and push to Confluence (owner: Diego, due Wed 04-15).
- Monitoring: Add explicit metrics for agent TLS handshake failures and MTU/fragmentation alerts to Console routing dashboard (owner: Marcus, due Fri 04-17).
- Quality guardrails: Optimize team to run quick evals on quantized model for AcmeHealth and create regression alert thresholds (owner: Priya from Optimize, pinged).

Notes for product/ops:
- We should consider a small, prebuilt 'airgap helper' artifact (tiny static binary + config) that customers can drop into environments that lack package managers. This would standardize our proxy-forwarder approach and reduce hand-holding. (Product idea: lightweight airgap agent).
- Add a short section in the sales playbook about typical network ask for Private installs: 443 outbound, ephemeral SSH for bastion tests, optional KMS endpoints (443), explicit list of required DN/URLs, and common rejection reasons (SNI blockers, strict egress).

Meeting decisions (summary):
- Proceed with quantization fallback for AcmeHealth initial rollout (customer approved).
- Add driver-compat testing to CI and delay wide rollout until compatibility validated for 535/CUDA12.
- Runbook to include proxy-forwarder pattern and CA install steps as standard for air-gapped installs.

Risks (for leadership):
- Short-term: throughput regressions for air-gapped installs that lack hardware crypto may cause missed SLAs; requires close monitoring and quick mitigations.
- Medium-term: if newer NVIDIA drivers become more common in customers' fleets, we need proactively supported images; otherwise we face repeated PoCs failing on driver mismatches.

Appendix: quick troubleshooting snippets (to be moved into runbook)

1) CA bundle installation (Debian)
- dpkg -i /tmp/redwood-certs.deb || apt-get install -f
- cp /tmp/customer-ca.pem /usr/local/share/ca-certificates/customer-ca.crt
- update-ca-certificates
- systemctl restart redwood-agent

2) Minimal proxy-forwarder systemd example (socat)
- /etc/systemd/system/redwood-proxy-forwarder.service
- ExecStart=/usr/bin/socat TCP-LISTEN:3128,fork TCP:proxy.internal:3128

3) MTU baseline check (customer host)
- ping -M do -s 1400 <agent-endpoint>
- if fragmentation occurs, ask net team to enable path MTU discovery or increase PMTU on TGW

Action log (quick):
- 2026-04-06: Created doc and started Monday standup (owner: Asha).
- 2026-04-07: CA handshake resolved for AcmeHealth; proxy-forwarder pattern agreed (owner: Diego).
- 2026-04-08: Customer chooses quantization fallback (owner: Lina).
- 2026-04-09: CI driver matrix jobs scheduled (owner: Marcus).
- 2026-04-10: Runbook draft merged; awaiting review (owners: Diego, Lina).

If anything here needs clarification or we should escalate a risk to Eng-Leadership, call it out in Slack #private-deploys and drop a link to this doc.

-- end of weekly check-in --
